sentences.en: What if it was a mistake from the start?
sentences.zh: 如果这一切从一开始就是一个错误呢？

sentences.en: The Declaration of Independence, the American Revolution, the creation of the United States of America.
sentences.zh: 《独立宣言》、美国革命、美利坚合众国的建立。

sentences.en: What if all this was a terrible idea?
sentences.zh: 如果这一切都是个糟糕的主意呢？

sentences.en: And what if the injustices and madness of American life since then have occurred not in spite of the virtues of the Founding Fathers, but because of them?
sentences.zh: 如果自那以后美国生活中出现的不公与疯狂，并非尽管有开国元勋们的美德，而是因为这些美德才发生的呢？

sentences.en: The revolution, this argument might run, was a needless and brutal bit of slaveholders' panic mixed with Enlightenment argle-bargle,
sentences.zh: 这种观点可能会认为，这场革命不过是一场毫无必要且残酷的奴隶主恐慌，混杂着启蒙运动的胡言乱语，

sentences.en: producing a country that was always marked for violence and disruption and demagogy.
sentences.zh: 造就了一个始终带有暴力、破坏和煽动色彩的国家。

sentences.en: Look north to Canada or south to Australia and you will see different possibilities of peaceful evolution away from Britain
sentences.zh: 看看北边的加拿大或南边的澳大利亚，你会看到脱离英国实现和平演变的不同可能性，

sentences.en: towards sane and whole, more equitable and less sanguinary countries.
sentences.zh: 走向理智、完整、更公平且流血更少的国家。

sentences.en: No revolution and slavery might have ended, as it did elsewhere in the British Empire, more peacefully and sooner.
sentences.zh: 如果没有那场革命，奴隶制或许能像大英帝国其他地方一样，更和平、更早地终结。

sentences.en: We could have ended with a social democratic commonwealth that stretched from north to south, a near continent-wide Canada.
sentences.zh: 我们本可以拥有一个从北到南的社会民主联邦，一个几乎覆盖整个大陆的加拿大。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So that, Tom, was Adam Gopnik, a very great essayist, in The New Yorker in May 2017, asking if the American Revolution was a mistake from the start.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，刚才那是亚当·戈普尼克，一位非常伟大的散文家，他在2017年5月的《纽约客》上提出了美国革命是否从一开始就是个错误的问题。

sentences.en: And of course, you and I will have our own opinions about whether or not it was a mistake.
sentences.zh: 当然，关于它是否是个错误，你和我会有各自的看法。

sentences.en: But the fact is that as we reach episode four of this mighty epic, we are in, what, 1778.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，当我们进入这部宏大史诗的第四集时，时间已经是1778年了。

sentences.en: The French and soon the Spanish have piled in, or in the Spanish case, will pile in.
sentences.zh: 法国人，以及很快加入的西班牙人，已经卷入其中，或者说在西班牙的案例中，即将卷入。

sentences.en: And they will be followed by other countries who form a League of Arm neutrality, the Russians, the Danes, the Prussians, the Austrians, the Portuguese,
sentences.zh: 随后会有其他国家加入，形成“武装中立联盟”，包括俄国人、丹麦人、普鲁士人、奥地利人、葡萄牙人，

sentences.en: basically making it very difficult for the British.
sentences.zh: 这基本上让英国人处境非常艰难。

sentences.en: And from this point, don't you think, Tom, the game is kind of up for Britain?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你不觉得从这一点来看，英国的大势已去了吗？

sentences.en: I think the game has been up right from the start.
sentences.zh: 我认为从一开始大势就已去了。

sentences.en: I don't think there was any prospect of the British ever.
sentences.zh: 我不认为英国人曾经有过任何胜算。

sentences.en: You think it was unwinnable from the beginning?
sentences.zh: 你认为从一开始这就是一场无法获胜的战争？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: So Adam Smith, Professor Adam Smith, who is the Edward Osborne Professor of American History at the University of Oxford, who has been performing manfully in these four episodes.
sentences.zh: 那么亚当·史密斯教授，他是牛津大学爱德华·奥斯本美国史教授，在这四集节目中表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: Adam, do you think the game was up from the very beginning?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你认为从一开始大势就已去了吗？

sentences.en: I think the game was up if the goal was a restoration of the status quo, as it had been before 1775.
sentences.zh: 如果目标是恢复1775年之前的现状，那么我认为大势已去。

sentences.en: I think other alternatives might have been possible.
sentences.zh: 但我认为其他选择或许是可能的。

sentences.en: I think if, you know, if we talked about in the previous episode, if Washington's army had been captured, if Saratoga hadn't fallen, I mean, there are other options.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在上一集讨论的那样，如果华盛顿的军队被俘，如果萨拉托加战役没有失利，我是说，还有其他选择。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the possibility is narrow and narrow and narrow.
sentences.zh: 但可能性越来越窄，越来越窄。

sentences.en: And definitely by the time you get to the French intervention,
sentences.zh: 而且到了法国干预的时候，

sentences.en: which is where we ended the last episode, it's very, very difficult to see how the British get out of this.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们上一集结束的地方，真的很难看出英国人该如何摆脱困境。

sentences.en: And yet the funny thing is you mentioned Washington.
sentences.zh: 然而有趣的是，你提到了华盛顿。

sentences.en: So Washington at this point, I mean, he's the great hero for the Americans, obviously, commander of the Continental Army.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿在这一点上，他是美国人心目中的大英雄，显然，他是大陆军的总司令。

sentences.en: At the point that the French get involved, he is really in the depths of sort of despondency, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 在法国人介入的时候，他其实正处于极度沮丧之中，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Philadelphia had been taken by the British and he has led his army into winter quarters at a place called Valley Forge,
sentences.zh: 因为费城被英国人占领了，他带领军队在福吉谷进入冬营，

sentences.en: which is about just under 20 miles northwest of Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 那里位于费城西北不到20英里处。

sentences.en: And he's there for six months and they've got nothing to eat.
sentences.zh: 他在那里待了六个月，他们什么吃的都没有。

sentences.en: It's freezing cold.
sentences.zh: 天气冷得要命。

sentences.en: They're really miserable.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很悲惨。

sentences.en: And Valley Forge is the sort of, so Ronald Reagan, big favorite of yours, Tom, of course.
sentences.zh: 福吉谷是那种——汤姆，罗纳德·里根可是你的最爱，当然。

sentences.en: Ronald Reagan used to tell this story about Washington kneeling in prayer at Valley Forge and asking God for help.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根过去常讲这个故事：华盛顿在福吉谷跪地祈祷，祈求上帝的帮助。

sentences.en: And Valley Forge is a really important part of the American mythology of the revolution and the war, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 福吉谷是美国革命和战争神话中非常重要的一部分，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's sort of, again, it's the underdog spirit.
sentences.zh: 因为它再次体现了那种弱者精神。

sentences.en: The odds are against us and, you know, God was with us.
sentences.zh: 我们处于劣势，你知道，上帝与我们同在。

sentences.en: Providence was with us.
sentences.zh: 天意与我们同在。

sentences.en: Do you think it really deserves that reputation, Adam?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你认为它真的配得上这种声誉吗？

sentences.en: Well, it was another moment when it's easy to imagine how the Continental Army could have completely dispersed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是另一个很容易想象大陆军会彻底溃散的时刻。

sentences.en: And if that had happened, the calculations would have shifted.
sentences.zh: 如果那样发生了，局势的计算就会改变。

sentences.en: It's not to say that there wouldn't have been some other kind of military force that would have been put together, perhaps under Washington, perhaps under somebody else.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说不会有其他形式的军事力量被组建起来，也许是在华盛顿的领导下，也许是在别人的领导下。

sentences.en: But it was certainly a desperate moment.
sentences.zh: 但这无疑是一个绝望的时刻。

sentences.en: And the reason, as you say, Dominic, I mean, the reason why it's become so much part of the myth of the American revolution in the United States
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，正如你所说，它之所以成为美国革命神话中如此重要的一部分，

sentences.en: is because it reinforces this underdog narrative and in that Reaganite way because it implies, at least, that it's only because of God's providence that it was possible
sentences.zh: 是因为它强化了这种弱者叙事，而且以那种里根式的方式，因为它至少暗示了，正是因为上帝的眷顾，美国人最终才有可能取得胜利。

sentences.en: in the end for the Americans to triumph.
sentences.zh: 上帝与女性。

sentences.en: God and women.
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 玛莎·华盛顿也在那里。

sentences.en: Martha Washington is there too.
sentences.zh: 她——我对玛莎·华盛顿了解不多，但她跟随了乔治。

sentences.en: She's – I don't know anything about Martha Washington, but she's followed George.
sentences.zh: 她在那里给人们包扎伤口，或者，我不知道，做汤什么的。

sentences.en: She's there sort of bandaging people and, I don't know, making soup or something.
sentences.zh: 听起来我对此有些轻率。

sentences.en: That sounds like I'm being flippant about.
sentences.zh: 但显然，女性从一开始就在美国革命中发挥了巨大作用，尤其是跟随她们的丈夫或男友随军。

sentences.en: But obviously women play a huge part in the American revolution from the beginning, not least in following their husbands or their boyfriends with the army.
sentences.zh: 她们在后方做了所有重要的事情，比如洗衣服、包扎伤口、提供食物，所有这些事情，

sentences.en: And they do all the important stuff behind the lines, like washing their clothes, bandaging their wounds, providing them with food, all those things,
sentences.zh: 这是一支军队绝对依赖的。

sentences.en: which an army absolutely depends on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，托马斯·潘恩对整个场景有一个精彩的描述，所有男人忙着修筑防御工事，女人们在劳作。

sentences.en: Well, Thomas Paine has a brilliant description of the whole setup with all the men who are busy building up the fortifications and the women laboring.
sentences.zh: 他说这就像一个海狸家庭。

sentences.en: And he says that it was like a family of beavers.
sentences.zh: 所以她们忙得不可开交。

sentences.en: So they're busy labelling away.
sentences.zh: 我知道你喜欢海狸，汤姆。

sentences.en: I know you like a beaver, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢海狸，没错。

sentences.en: I love a beaver, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但亚当，关于美国革命中的女性，我们还没怎么谈过，但她们——我是说，现在的史学界确实非常强调女性所扮演的角色，

sentences.en: But Adam, so women in the American revolution, we haven't talked about women much, but they are – I mean, historiography now really plays up the part that women played
sentences.zh: 这在100年前是不可能的情况。

sentences.en: in a way that wouldn't have been the case 100 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且至关重要，因为正如我们一直在强调的那样，这场战争的胜负取决于美国白人殖民公众及其对这一事业的承诺。

sentences.en: And critically so, because this was a war which, as we've in effect been emphasising, was won or lost by the American white colonial public and their commitment to this cause.
sentences.zh: 因此，正是在美国家庭中做出了牺牲，做出了承诺，试图熬过这段考验时期，红衫军的存在，

sentences.en: And so it was in American households that sacrifices were made, that commitments were made to try to wait out this – through this time of trial, the presence of the Redcoats,
sentences.zh: 军队本身的存在加强了美国人试图——但唯一可能带来荣誉的结果就是彻底的胜利，彻底的独立，

sentences.en: the presence of the army in itself intensified American commitment to try to – but the only possible outcome with any honour was complete victory, complete independence,
sentences.zh: 永远将英军从美国土地上清除出去。

sentences.en: removing British troops forever from American soil.
sentences.zh: 乔治国王已经被拉下马了。

sentences.en: King George had already been taken down.
sentences.zh: 如果只关注军队中的男人和做出决定的将军，以及那些当然都是男人的开国元勋，这一切都无法解释。

sentences.en: None of that is explicable if the only focus is on the men in the armies and the generals making the decisions on the American side
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，不是有一段著名的通信吗？

sentences.en: and the founding fathers who are all, of course, men.
sentences.zh: 阿比盖尔·亚当斯——是阿比盖尔·亚当斯吗？

sentences.en: But, of course, isn't there a famous exchange of letters,
sentences.zh: 是的，约翰·亚当斯的妻子，没错。

sentences.en: Abigail Adams – is it Abigail Adams?
sentences.zh: 她在他们通过《独立宣言》时写信给他，说，你知道，当你们重塑世界时，也要考虑一下女性。

sentences.en: Yes, John Adams' wife, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不要忘记女士们。

sentences.en: Where she writes to him when they're passing the Declaration of Independence and says, you know, while you're remaking the world, think about women as well.
sentences.zh: 不要忘记女士们。

sentences.en: Do not forget the ladies.
sentences.zh: 他以一种极其傲慢的方式回信说，是啊，没错，你知道，好像我们会那样做一样，

sentences.en: Do not forget the ladies.
sentences.zh: 好像我们会花一秒钟去考虑你们似的。

sentences.en: And he sort of writes back in this incredibly condescending way and says, yeah, right, you know, like we're going to do that,
sentences.zh: 所以曾经有过——他确实是这么做的。

sentences.en: like we're going to give you a second's thought or something.
sentences.zh: 不过公平地说，那实际上是一段精彩的通信。

sentences.en: So was there ever – He does, he does.
sentences.zh: 我是说，约翰和阿比盖尔·亚当斯互相写信。

sentences.en: Although, in fairness, I mean, that's actually a magnificent exchange of letters.
sentences.zh: 在整个革命危机期间，他们大部分时间都是分开的。

sentences.en: I mean, John and Abigail Adams write to each other.
sentences.zh: 他显然非常看重她，把她当作一种顾问和建议来源。

sentences.en: They're apart most of the time throughout this whole revolutionary crisis.
sentences.zh: 他会和她探讨想法，想知道她的想法，以及她周围波士顿的人们在想什么。

sentences.en: And he clearly takes her incredibly seriously as a kind of counsellor and source of advice.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是一段非常令人印象深刻且有趣的亲密政治关系，也是一段情感关系。

sentences.en: And he tests out ideas with her and he wants to know what she thinks and what people around her back in Boston are thinking.
sentences.zh: 那么，对于女性、穷人、奴隶，对于那些被推向美国政治生活边缘的人来说，

sentences.en: So it's actually quite a really impressive and interesting close political relationship as well as emotional one between John and Abigail.
sentences.zh: 是否可能有一个更进步的结果呢？

sentences.en: So could there have been a more, as it were, a more progressive outcome for women, for the poor, for slaves, for people who are pushed to the margins
sentences.zh: 还是说它注定会像那样发展？

sentences.en: of kind of American political life?
sentences.zh: 但是——我是说，战争对奴隶来说不是挺糟糕的吗，因为他们被视为站在了英国人一边。

sentences.en: Or was it always going to play out as it did?
sentences.zh: 所以某种程度上，压迫结构因为革命战争而变得更加紧密了。

sentences.en: But doesn't – I mean, doesn't – the war is kind of bad for slaves because they are seen as having sided with the British.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in a way, the kind of the structures of oppression become – are tightened as a result of the Revolutionary War.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为性别和阶级在美国革命中与种族的作用方式不同。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在1790年代，确实有一个时刻女性获得了选举权。

sentences.en: Well, I think gender and class work out in different ways from race in the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 在新泽西州，众所周知，如果她们是业主，她们几乎是偶然地获得了选举权，一些女性，极少数女性。

sentences.en: And there is a moment in the 1790s when women are enfranchised.
sentences.zh: 就贫穷的白人男性而言，美国革命在几乎所有地方都是一大福音。

sentences.en: In New Jersey, famously, they're kind of almost accidentally enfranchised if they're property owners, some women, a tiny number of women.
sentences.zh: 大约在那个时候编写的一些新州宪法，宾夕法尼亚州是最好的例子，

sentences.en: In terms of poor white men, the American Revolution was almost everywhere a great boon.
sentences.zh: 是非常激进的宪法，赋予了普通白人、无产者相对于世界上任何其他地方而言巨大的权力，

sentences.en: And some of the new state constitutions that are being written around about this time, Pennsylvania being the best example,
sentences.zh: 或者说除了1640年代英国革命最激进的极端时刻外，世界上任何地方都从未真正梦想过。

sentences.en: are incredibly radical constitutions that give huge amounts of power to ordinary white, propertyless men relative to anywhere else in the world
sentences.zh: 那么，比如说印第安人，也就是美洲原住民呢？

sentences.en: or that really has ever been properly dreamed of anywhere in the world other than, you know, the most radical extreme moments of the English Revolution of the 1640s.
sentences.zh: 英国人正试图招募美洲原住民作为盟友。

sentences.en: What about, let's say, Indians, so Native Americans?
sentences.zh: 事实上，在整个这一时期，西部边境，也就是那种前沿地带，发生了非常血腥的战斗。

sentences.en: So the British are trying to enlist Native Americans as allies.
sentences.zh: 美国革命对他们来说结果是好是坏？

sentences.en: And in fact, throughout all this period, there's very bloody fighting in the Western borderlands, the kind of frontier zone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，我猜你会有什么答案。

sentences.en: Does the American Revolution work out well or badly?
sentences.zh: 答案是对美洲原住民来说并不好。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I'm guessing what your answer is going to be.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们以前被视为像其他人一样的乔治国王的臣民，但现在他们被视为敌人了吗？

sentences.en: The answer is not well for Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是因为我们在第一集讨论的原因，伦敦的决策者试图平衡

sentences.en: And is that because previously they had just been seen as King George's subjects like any others, but now they are seen as enemies?
sentences.zh: 北美强大的土著民族与白人定居者之间的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess for the reasons we were talking about in the first episode, it was in the interest of policymakers in London to try to balance
sentences.zh: 法国人也做了同样的事情。

sentences.en: the powerful indigenous nations in North America against white settlers.
sentences.zh: 法国人正在与美洲原住民结盟。

sentences.en: And the French did the same.
sentences.zh: 美国独立的实际影响是，美洲原住民被视为

sentences.en: The French were making alliances with Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 在新建立的美国边界内基本上是可以随意处置的对象。

sentences.en: The practical effects of American independence was that Native American peoples were then regarded
sentences.zh: 不，从原住民的角度来看，美国革命显然是一件坏事。

sentences.en: as being essentially fair game within the boundaries of the newly established United States.
sentences.zh: 亚当，接着这一点说，美洲原住民被视为与英国人结盟，

sentences.en: And no, the American Revolution was clearly a bad thing from the point of view of indigenous people.
sentences.zh: 而南方奴隶的情况想必更是如此，

sentences.en: And Adam, just to follow up on that, that the Native Americans are seen as having allied themselves
sentences.zh: 他们不仅逃离了主人，在某些情况下甚至加入了英军。

sentences.en: with the British, and presumably even more so that's the case with slaves in the South
sentences.zh: 所以有一个著名的埃塞俄比亚军团，就是这么叫的。

sentences.en: who have not only escaped their owners, but in certain cases have actually joined the British Army.
sentences.zh: 还有一个黑人龙骑兵中队被编入英军。

sentences.en: So there's a famous Ethiopian regiment, it's called.
sentences.zh: 黑人保皇党发挥了重要作用，但在过去几十年的美国史学中，这个角色并没有被深入探讨。

sentences.en: And then there's a squad of black dragoons who are enrolled in the British Army.
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚军团，我认为最初是由邓莫尔勋爵组建的，是我们上一集讨论过的公告的直接后果。

sentences.en: Black loyalists play an important role and not a role that's dwelt in traditionally in American historiography until the last couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 埃塞俄比亚军团的一名士兵，哈里·华盛顿，曾是乔治·华盛顿的奴隶，出生在冈比亚，在战争前10到15年被华盛顿买下，

sentences.en: And the Ethiopian regiment, I think, was originally raised by Lord Dunmore and was a direct consequence of the proclamation that we talked about in a previous episode.
sentences.zh: 当他听到邓莫尔的公告时逃跑了，并在整个革命战争期间为国王而战，

sentences.en: One of the soldiers in the Ethiopian regiment, Harry Washington, was owned by George Washington, being born in the Gambia, purchased by Washington some 10 or 15 years
sentences.zh: 我认为他最终是那些被英国人撤离并定居在诺瓦斯科舍省的黑人保皇党之一。

sentences.en: before the war, ran away when he heard of Dunmore's proclamation and fought for the king
sentences.zh: 那句话是怎么说的，有时自由穿着红外套什么的？

sentences.en: throughout the Revolutionary War, was eventually, I think, among those black loyalists who were evacuated by the British and settled in Nova Scotia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，只是随口一提，给我们的美国听众。

sentences.en: So what was it, the phrase, sometimes liberty wears a red coat or something?
sentences.zh: 是的，肯定没有美国听众留下来了。

sentences.en: Well, just throwing that out, our American listeners.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们回到对美国听众来说更令人高兴的事情，即英国战争努力的逐渐崩溃。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are surely no American listeners left.
sentences.zh: 我们上一集结束于1778年2月，法国人卷入其中。

sentences.en: So let's get back to something that will be cheerier for American listeners, namely the gradual implosion of the British war effort.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人一年后也加入了。

sentences.en: So we ended the last episode, February 1778, the French piling in.
sentences.zh: 正如我们之前所说，这显然彻底改变了动态。

sentences.en: The Spanish have joined a year later.
sentences.zh: 因为他们想把战争扩大。

sentences.en: And that obviously, as we were saying before, completely changes the dynamic.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这基本上就是他们想要的。

sentences.en: Because they want to brought it back.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, that's basically what they want.
sentences.zh: 但当然，对英国人来说，这不仅仅是保卫加勒比地区的问题。

sentences.en: The Spanish do indeed.
sentences.zh: 他们也知道如何保卫英国。

sentences.en: But of course, for the British, it's not just defending the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 我是说，亚当，法国入侵的可能性，我想，并不大，但也不是可以忽略不计的。

sentences.en: They also know how to defend Britain.
sentences.zh: 我是说，英国人在这一时期总是担心法国入侵，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, so Adam, the chances of a French invasion, I suppose, they're not enormous, but they're not negligible either.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the British are always worried about a French invasion in this period, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这不仅仅是理论上的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，有1779年的无敌舰队。

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't just theoretical.
sentences.zh: 所以法国和西班牙联合海军进行了一次尝试，

sentences.en: There was an armada, the armada of 1779, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 至少试图让英国从美洲、加勒比地区以及英国试图保卫的所有其他地方的战争中分心，

sentences.en: So there was an attempt by a combined French and Spanish navy,
sentences.zh: 但你知道，确实存在登陆大不列颠的真实前景。

sentences.en: attempted at the very least to kind of divert Britain from the war in the Americas and in the Caribbean and all these other places Britain was trying to defend.
sentences.zh: 而这方面最著名的海军创新是，法国政府委托了一位名叫约翰·保罗·琼斯的美国人，

sentences.en: But, you know, with a genuine prospect of landing in Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名奴隶船船长，去袭击英国海岸，他确实取得了一些成功。

sentences.en: And the most famous kind of naval innovation in this is that the French government commissions an American called John Paul Jones,
sentences.zh: 而这其中最著名的海军创新形式，是法国政府委任了一位名叫约翰·保罗·琼斯的美国人，

sentences.en: who's a kind of former slave ship captain, to actually go and raid the British coast, which he does with some success.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名奴隶船船长，受命去突袭英国海岸，并且取得了一定的成功。

sentences.en: Whitehaven.
sentences.zh: 怀特黑文。

sentences.en: Yeah, he shells Whitehaven and Cumberland.
sentences.zh: 没错，他炮轰了怀特黑文和坎伯兰。

sentences.en: He's still quite remembered there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里至今仍被人们铭记。

sentences.en: If you go to Whitehaven, where there is, by the way, an excellent secondhand bookshop,
sentences.zh: 如果你去怀特黑文，顺便提一下，那里有一家很棒的二手书店，

sentences.en: John Paul Jones is still remembered in Whitehaven, and rightly so.
sentences.zh: 约翰·保罗·琼斯在怀特黑文依然被人铭记，这是理所应当的。

sentences.en: And he ends up taking shelter in the Netherlands, which I think reflects very poorly on the Dutch that they allowed him in.
sentences.zh: 他最终在荷兰避难，我认为荷兰人允许他入境，这让他们显得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So his life then takes a series of very bizarre twists, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以他的人生随后经历了一系列非常离奇的转折，汤姆。

sentences.en: He ends up in Russia after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他最终去了俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He's accused of raping a 10-year-old girl.
sentences.zh: 他被指控强奸了一名10岁的小女孩。

sentences.en: And he goes to Poland, and then he goes back to Paris, and he ends up being made U.S.
sentences.zh: 后来他去了波兰，又回到了巴黎，最终被任命为美国驻阿尔及尔领事。

sentences.en: consul in Algiers.
sentences.zh: 领事。

sentences.en: Of course, yes, of course he does.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的，他当然会那样。

sentences.en: Yes, against the slavers.
sentences.zh: 是的，去对抗那些奴隶贩子。

sentences.en: But then dies before he can take up his – he's found dead in his Paris apartment.
sentences.zh: 但他还没来得及上任就去世了——人们发现他死在巴黎的公寓里。

sentences.en: Isn't that a strange life?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是一段离奇的人生吗？

sentences.en: There's the plot of a thriller.
sentences.zh: 这简直是惊悚小说的情节。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's all part of the – So that's not good for anybody.
sentences.zh: 总之，这都是其中的一部分——所以这对任何人来说都不是好事。

sentences.en: Well, it's not good for the people of Whitehaven, I think it's what you say, Adam.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你说得对，亚当，这对怀特黑文的人民来说确实不是好事。

sentences.en: But the British still have a – the amazing thing is they don't give in.
sentences.zh: 但英国人依然有一种——令人惊奇的是，他们没有放弃。

sentences.en: They don't just say, right, let's just cut our losses.
sentences.zh: 他们没有直接说，好吧，让我们及时止损吧。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Why do we keep going?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们还要坚持下去？

sentences.en: Just pride?
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为自尊心吗？

sentences.en: Stubbornness?
sentences.zh: 还是固执？

sentences.en: I think yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think those things.
sentences.zh: 我想是这些原因。

sentences.en: I mean, that really is a great question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这确实是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Because by this point, you know, the support in the House of Commons for Lord North is ebbing away.
sentences.zh: 因为到了这个时候，你知道，下议院对诺斯勋爵的支持正在减弱。

sentences.en: It starts losing some critical votes.
sentences.zh: 他开始输掉一些关键的投票。

sentences.en: I mean, there are plenty of people in Britain by this point saying, let's cut our losses and get out.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时英国有很多人说，让我们及时止损，撤出来吧。

sentences.en: But it's a massive thing.
sentences.zh: 但这是一件大事。

sentences.en: It's a massive thing to acknowledge the independence of these 13 colonies, you know.
sentences.zh: 承认这13个殖民地的独立是一件大事，你知道的。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, as late as 1780, Britain is still winning victories.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，直到1780年，英国仍在赢得胜利。

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 他们确实在赢。

sentences.en: So they win the Battle of Camden, which for any Londoner is a kind of an amusing idea.
sentences.zh: 所以他们赢得了卡姆登战役，这对任何伦敦人来说都是一个有点好笑的想法。

sentences.en: That's South Carolina, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是南卡罗来纳州，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes, South Carolina, not in North London.
sentences.zh: 是的，南卡罗来纳州，不是北伦敦。

sentences.en: And they're fighting in the South because there is – and actually, this is a good answer to your question, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 他们在南方作战，因为——事实上，这对你的问题是一个很好的回答，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I mean, as Tom is implying there, there is still this thought, well, maybe we can turn this around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如汤姆刚才暗示的那样，人们仍然有这种想法，嗯，也许我们可以扭转局面。

sentences.en: And they're fighting in the South, not least because in the South they have good reason to believe there are still lots of loyalists there.
sentences.zh: 他们在南方作战，很大程度上是因为在南方，他们有充分的理由相信那里仍然有很多效忠派。

sentences.en: And there are.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: There are loyalist groups who are irregular forces who are fighting to try to support the British.
sentences.zh: 有一些效忠派团体，也就是那些试图支持英国的非正规武装力量。

sentences.en: And so the famous story of an American independence fighter who gets turned, of course, is Benedict Arnold.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个著名的美国独立战士被策反的故事，当然就是本尼迪克特·阿诺德。

sentences.en: And he is – so what was he?
sentences.zh: 他——那么他是什么样的人？

sentences.en: He was a kind of very distinguished general, kind of very energetic general, kind of loses his mobility.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常杰出的将军，非常有活力，但后来失去了行动能力。

sentences.en: He gets badly injured in his legs, but is still very kind of feisty.
sentences.zh: 他的腿受了重伤，但依然非常有斗志。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And feels that he's not getting the credit that he's owed.
sentences.zh: 而且他觉得他没有得到应有的认可。

sentences.en: Yes, he's not being promoted because he's from the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 是的，他没有得到晋升，因为他出身不对。

sentences.en: And there's all this business about the Continental Congress wanting to share out the commissions among the different states and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 还有大陆会议想要在不同州之间分配军衔之类的所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And he's clearly a kind of prickly, ambitious figure who doesn't think he's getting his fair dues.
sentences.zh: 他显然是一个脾气暴躁、雄心勃勃的人物，认为自己没有得到公平的待遇。

sentences.en: He's also married to a beautiful woman, Peggy Shippen, who was a loyalist from a loyalist family anyway in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 他还娶了一位美丽的妻子，佩吉·希彭，她本身就来自费城的一个效忠派家庭。

sentences.en: And he, as you say, he gets turned and he thinks, actually, maybe I could get more accolades and get more glory if I defect to the British side.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他被策反了，他想，其实如果我投靠英国，也许能获得更多的赞誉和荣耀。

sentences.en: And it goes wrong from his point of view.
sentences.zh: 但从他的角度来看，事情搞砸了。

sentences.en: I mean, he ends up – he survives.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他最终——他活了下来。

sentences.en: Because he gets offered the command of West Point, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他被提议担任西点军校的指挥官，不是吗？

sentences.en: And it's suggested that he – He does, and he's going to surrender.
sentences.zh: 有人建议他——他确实被提议了，而且他打算投降。

sentences.en: The plan is he's going to surrender West Point to the British.
sentences.zh: 计划是他要将西点军校交给英国人。

sentences.en: But the plan is exposed before he can do that.
sentences.zh: 但在他实施之前，计划就暴露了。

sentences.en: He manages to escape.
sentences.zh: 他设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: His wife, Peggy, eventually manages to escape as well.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子佩吉最终也设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: And they're reunited in London.
sentences.zh: 他们在伦敦团聚了。

sentences.en: But the guy who'd been running the messages, Major John Andre, is captured by the Americans.
sentences.zh: 但是那个负责传递消息的人，约翰·安德烈少校，被美国人抓住了。

sentences.en: And he's British, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他是英国人，对吧？

sentences.en: And he is British.
sentences.zh: 他确实是英国人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's executed as a spy.
sentences.zh: 他被当作间谍处决了。

sentences.en: And he's hung.
sentences.zh: 他被绞死了。

sentences.en: He's not shot, as a gentleman should be, but he's hung.
sentences.zh: 他没有像绅士那样被枪决，而是被绞死了。

sentences.en: And even the Americans who capture him and are holding him prisoner in the weeks before he's executed, think they just swoon over this guy.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些俘虏他并在他被处决前几周关押他的美国人，都对他倾倒不已。

sentences.en: They think John Andre is the most magnificent military figure.
sentences.zh: 他们认为约翰·安德烈是最出色的军事人物。

sentences.en: Astonishing, bearing, good-looking, brave.
sentences.zh: 风度惊人，长相英俊，勇敢无畏。

sentences.en: And when he walks out into his final execution, and he's still astonished because he thinks he's going to be shot until he sees the noose hanging there.
sentences.zh: 当他走向最后的刑场时，他依然感到震惊，因为他以为自己会被枪决，直到他看到悬挂在那里的绞索。

sentences.en: And he's asked if he wants to say any last words.
sentences.zh: 有人问他是否有遗言。

sentences.en: And he says, bear me witness that I bear my fate like a brave man.
sentences.zh: 他说，请为我作证，我像个勇敢的人一样面对命运。

sentences.en: And they all go, oh, how magnificent.
sentences.zh: 他们都说，哦，多么壮烈。

sentences.en: So there's absolutely a sense still that the Americans are capable of admiring officers in the British Army.
sentences.zh: 所以，美国人依然能够钦佩英国军队中的军官，这种感觉是绝对存在的。

sentences.en: But equally, there is also a figure who is up there in the annals of infamy alongside Benedict Arnold, who is a British officer called Banastre Tarleton.
sentences.zh: 但同样，在臭名昭著的名单上，还有一位与本尼迪克特·阿诺德齐名的人物，他是一位名叫伯纳斯特·塔尔顿的英国军官。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 才华横溢。

sentences.en: And he is the guy who inspires, what's his name, in The Patriot.
sentences.zh: 他就是电影《爱国者》中那个角色的灵感来源，叫什么名字来着？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: The kind of villainous.
sentences.zh: 那种恶棍。

sentences.en: Mel Gibson's villain.
sentences.zh: 梅尔·吉布森电影里的那个反派。

sentences.en: But he's a tremendous man, isn't he, Banastre Tarleton?
sentences.zh: 但他是个了不起的人，不是吗，伯纳斯特·塔尔顿？

sentences.en: He looks gallant.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很英勇。

sentences.en: He kind of looks the part.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很有派头。

sentences.en: And he kind of wins the battle, and his opponents surrender, and then all his men slash them and kill them.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了战斗，对手投降了，然后他的人马把他们砍杀殆尽。

sentences.en: And so this is Tarleton's quarter, it's called.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“塔尔顿的仁慈”。

sentences.en: The Tarleton complained that he'd been actually, his horse had been shot from under him, and he'd been stuck under the horse, so he wasn't in a position to help out.
sentences.zh: 塔尔顿抱怨说，实际上他的马被击中倒下，他被压在马下，所以他没法帮忙。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you could argue, couldn't you, Tom, to go back to the thing we were talking about in previous episodes,
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，你可以争辩说，不是吗，汤姆，回到我们之前几集讨论的话题，

sentences.en: that if the British Army had had rather more Tarletons and fewer gentleman Johnnies or whatever they were called,
sentences.zh: 如果英国军队有更多的塔尔顿，而少一些所谓的“绅士约翰尼”之类的人，

sentences.en: then maybe they would have done a bit better than sort of playing by the Queensby rules, which they're sort of doing throughout.
sentences.zh: 那么也许他们会比一直以来那种按部就班的打法做得更好。

sentences.en: Is that fair, Adam?
sentences.zh: 这样说公平吗，亚当？

sentences.en: Or am I being too ruthless?
sentences.zh: 还是我太冷酷了？

sentences.en: Well, it certainly would have created a different outcome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这肯定会产生不同的结果。

sentences.en: But, you know, as we were saying before, all the time the British are saying, well, you know, it's a hearts and minds strategy, and they just don't quite bring themselves in it.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，正如我们之前所说，英国人一直都在说，嗯，你知道，这是一种“争取民心”的策略，但他们就是没能真正做到。

sentences.en: And really, if every British general had been a bloody Ben Tarleton, I mean, is it going to fundamentally change the story?
sentences.zh: 说真的，如果每个英国将军都是个该死的本·塔尔顿，我的意思是，这会从根本上改变故事吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it is.
sentences.zh: 我不认为会。

sentences.en: All it would have done is to really even further entrench.
sentences.zh: 它只会让情况更加根深蒂固。

sentences.en: Poison relations, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 毒化了关系，不是吗？

sentences.en: Just to go back to the question I asked 10 minutes ago, which was about why Britain kept fighting, why Britain didn't throw.
sentences.zh: 回到我10分钟前问的问题，关于为什么英国坚持战斗，为什么英国没有放弃。

sentences.en: I suppose one answer is that the British, I mean, nobody knows how the story will end.
sentences.zh: 我想一个答案是，英国人——我的意思是，没人知道故事会如何结束。

sentences.en: So nobody knows that all 13 colonies will become independent.
sentences.zh: 所以没人知道所有13个殖民地最终都会独立。

sentences.en: And as you said, there are still lots of loyalists in, let's say, South Carolina or North Carolina or wherever.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你所说，在南卡罗来纳、北卡罗来纳或其他地方，仍然有很多效忠派。

sentences.en: So perhaps do the British think, you know what, the South is quite lucrative with its plantations.
sentences.zh: 所以也许英国人会想，你知道吗，南方有种植园，利润相当可观。

sentences.en: We could keep those states.
sentences.zh: 我们可以保留那些州。

sentences.en: I don't know where ever, but Virginia, the Carolinas.
sentences.zh: 我不知道具体是哪里，但弗吉尼亚、卡罗来纳地区。

sentences.en: Well, because, of course, with the French entering the war, there's the risk that the Caribbean colonies might go as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为当然，随着法国参战，加勒比海殖民地也有可能丢失。

sentences.en: And the British are facing the prospect of losing all their colonies in the new world.
sentences.zh: 英国人面临着失去他们在“新世界”所有殖民地的风险。

sentences.en: So the fact that they're able to hold on to their Caribbean colonies suggests that that's not entirely a foolish strategy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以他们能够守住加勒比海殖民地这一事实，说明这并非完全是愚蠢的策略，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I think, yes, they're always trying to hold on to the Caribbean colonies, number one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是的，他们首先总是试图守住加勒比海殖民地。

sentences.en: And in a way, the fact that everybody's ganged up on Britain, is that effectively revenge, as it were, for the Seven Years' War?
sentences.zh: 这是否承认七年战争让英国处于一种被攻击的卓越地位？

sentences.en: And is that recognition that the Seven Years' War had put Britain up there to be shot at in a kind of preeminent position?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我觉得你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常可怕的时刻。

sentences.en: And it's a really scary moment.
sentences.zh: 伦敦的人们，他们真正害怕的是这种在欧洲的孤立。

sentences.en: People in London, that's what they were really frightened of, is this isolation in Europe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为整个18世纪到19世纪，英国的外交政策都是为了避免，

sentences.en: You know, because all of British foreign policy through the 18th century is to avoid, and into the 19th century,
sentences.zh: 避免在18世纪70年代末和80年代初发生的那种在欧洲的孤立。

sentences.en: is to avoid isolation in Europe of the kind that happens in the late 1770s and early 1780s.
sentences.zh: 他们不想让这种情况再次发生。

sentences.en: And they don't want that to happen again.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国决策者吸取的教训。

sentences.en: That's the lesson the British policymakers draw.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，英国，我觉得公平地说——显然，我知道我们剩下的美国听众会说，我这辈子没听过这么偏袒的播客，

sentences.en: But actually, so Britain, I think it's fair to say, I mean, obviously, I know our remaining American listener will say, I've never heard such a partisan podcast in my life,
sentences.zh: 简直是胡说八道。

sentences.en: Triopic Tosh.
sentences.zh: 但公平地说，英国从本系列开始到这一刻，犯了一系列非常严重的错误。

sentences.en: But it's fair to say that the British have made a series of very bad mistakes from the start of this series to right to this point.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，英国在和平谈判中确实表现出色，不是吗？

sentences.en: But in a weird way, the British really distinguish themselves with the piece, don't they?
sentences.zh: 因为他们让美国人签署了和平协议。

sentences.en: Because they get the Americans to sign a piece.
sentences.zh: 他们与英国单独达成协议，并且给予美国人比法国或西班牙想要的更慷慨的条款。

sentences.en: They do a deal with the British alone, and they give the Americans much more generous terms than the French or the Spanish want them to.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林在巴黎进行谈判，对吧？

sentences.en: And Franklin's negotiating it in Paris, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常自由的谈判者。

sentences.en: And he's a kind of very free-form negotiator.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英国人说，我们这样做吧。

sentences.en: You know, the British say, let's do this.
sentences.zh: 他说，好啊，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: And he goes, yeah, why not?
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 《巴黎条约》的故事通常被描述为富兰克林谈判技巧的伟大胜利。

sentences.en: The story of the Treaty of Paris is usually told as a great triumph for Franklin's negotiating skills.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，美国人确实做得很好。

sentences.en: And no doubt the Americans did do a good job.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，这是因为英国绝对不需要同意给新成立的美国如此慷慨的条款。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, what this is about is that the British definitely did not need to agree such generous terms to the new United States.
sentences.zh: 但这样做符合英国的利益。

sentences.en: But it was in Britain's interest to do that.
sentences.zh: 一旦失去了13个殖民地，符合英国利益的是在北美拥有一个相对强大的美国，作为对抗法国的堡垒。

sentences.en: Once the 13 colonies had been lost, it was in Britain's interest to have a reasonably strong United States in North America as a bulwark against the French.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且还要留住他们，大概是为了留住他们，因为还有加拿大和加勒比地区。

sentences.en: And also to keep them, presumably to keep them on board because there's Canada and there's the Caribbean as well.
sentences.zh: 确实，确实。

sentences.en: Indeed, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实，确实。

sentences.en: And, you know, the worst outcome in the Treaty of Paris for Britain would have been France reclaiming some of her possessions in North America or Spain doing likewise.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于英国来说，巴黎条约最糟糕的结果莫过于法国收回其在北美的一些属地，或者西班牙也这样做。

sentences.en: And so a weak, fragmented, tiny United States just clinging to the Atlantic seaboard, which would have been certain to invite another war very soon,
sentences.zh: 因此，一个虚弱、分裂、渺小，只能依附于大西洋沿岸的美国，肯定很快就会招致另一场战争，

sentences.en: that wouldn't have been in Britain's interest either.
sentences.zh: 这对英国来说也不是什么好事。

sentences.en: So long as they wanted to hold, as you say, Tom, as long as they wanted to hold on to their possessions in Canada.
sentences.zh: 只要他们想守住，正如你所说的，汤姆，只要他们想守住自己在加拿大的属地。

sentences.en: And just on, I mean, people will often talk about what the Americans call the Revolutionary War and we call it the American War of Independence.
sentences.zh: 而且，人们经常谈论美国人所说的“革命战争”，而我们称之为“美国独立战争”。

sentences.en: People often talk of it as a civil war.
sentences.zh: 人们常把它称为一场内战。

sentences.en: When it's over, I mean, when they are meeting Franklin, who, you know, used to play chess with British guys when he was in London before the war, is there bad blood?
sentences.zh: 战争结束后，当他们见到富兰克林时——你知道，他在战前在伦敦时常和英国人下棋——他们之间会有积怨吗？

sentences.en: Or are they all sort of shaking hands and drinking port and kind of chuckling about, you know, funny things that happened at Saratoga or whatever?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们都在握手言欢，喝着波特酒，谈笑风生，聊着萨拉托加战役中发生的趣事之类的？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the sort of atmosphere like between Britain and America in the immediate aftermath?
sentences.zh: 我是说，战争刚结束时，英国和美国之间的气氛如何？

sentences.en: There's a very emotional moment when John Adams comes to London as the first minister from the new United States and he's presented at court and he has a conversation with the king and they're both very emotional about this and the king certainly so.
sentences.zh: 当约翰·亚当斯作为新美国的首位公使来到伦敦时，有一个非常感人的时刻。他在宫廷受到接见，并与国王进行了交谈，他们对此都非常动情，国王尤其如此。

sentences.en: But John Adams pledges the future friendship of the United States and emphasizes all the common ties of culture and language and religion.
sentences.zh: 但约翰·亚当斯承诺了美国未来的友谊，并强调了文化、语言和宗教方面的所有共同纽带。

sentences.en: And with the strong implication that now this late unpleasantness is behind us, at the end of the day, we are now like you and like we've always been a great Protestant power.
sentences.zh: 并强烈暗示，既然这些最近的不愉快已经过去，归根结底，我们现在就像你们一样，也像我们一直以来那样，是一个伟大的新教强国。

sentences.en: And we know who our enemies are, they're the French.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道我们的敌人是谁，那就是法国人。

sentences.en: And that was why Thomas Jefferson, in contrast, did not go down so well in London.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么相比之下，托马斯·杰斐逊在伦敦并不那么受欢迎。

sentences.en: So the answer to your question, Dominic, is it depends on which Americans you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，回答你的问题，这取决于你指的是哪些美国人。

sentences.en: Because Jefferson is a shameless Francophile, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为杰斐逊是个厚颜无耻的亲法派，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is and he remains a shameless Francophile even into the 1790s.
sentences.zh: 他是，而且即使到了18世纪90年代，他依然是个厚颜无耻的亲法派。

sentences.en: As the guillotine is falling, Jefferson is toasting the Chateau of the Loire and whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 当断头台落下时，杰斐逊还在为卢瓦尔河谷的城堡之类的东西举杯祝酒。

sentences.en: So one of the famous paradoxes of history is that actually the real impact of the American Revolution falls on France rather than on Britain because French support for the American war effort bleeds them so much money that it precipitates the revolution.
sentences.zh: 所以历史著名的悖论之一是，实际上美国革命对法国的影响比对英国的影响更大，因为法国对美国战争努力的支持耗尽了他们的钱财，从而加速了法国大革命的爆发。

sentences.en: And you talked about America being Protestant,
sentences.zh: 你刚才谈到美国是新教国家，

sentences.en: but one of the other interesting kind of corollaries of the war period is that Jefferson is able to make the case for there being kind of wide scale religious tolerance.
sentences.zh: 但战争时期另一个有趣的推论是，杰斐逊能够为实现广泛的宗教宽容提供理由。

sentences.en: And that is something that simply because the structures of kind of establishment churches are no longer able to be maintained.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为国教的结构已无法维持。

sentences.en: And so that's another very, very significant fruit of the of the Revolutionary War, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这也是革命战争另一个非常、非常重要的成果，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, pretty much everybody imagines that the religious toleration is within a Protestant context.
sentences.zh: 我是说，几乎每个人都认为这种宗教宽容是在新教背景下的。

sentences.en: It's a different matter being entirely tolerant of Catholics and never mind non-Christians.
sentences.zh: 对天主教徒完全宽容是另一回事，更不用说非基督徒了。

sentences.en: But once it's been kind of written into the Constitution, then, you know, a bit like the Declaration of Independence, you know,
sentences.zh: 但一旦它被写入宪法，那么，你知道，就像《独立宣言》一样，你知道，

sentences.en: these are slow burners that will burn their way through American history.
sentences.zh: 这些都是缓慢燃烧的火种，它们将贯穿整个美国历史。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And disestablishment happens across the new United States in those places that still have a church establishment quite quickly afterwards.
sentences.zh: 而且在那些仍然拥有国教的新美国各地，政教分离很快就发生了。

sentences.en: Massachusetts is the last, I believe, is the last state to disestablish its church.
sentences.zh: 我相信马萨诸塞州是最后一个废除其国教的州。

sentences.en: So they hold the Puritan tradition clings on there for a long time.
sentences.zh: 所以他们坚持清教徒传统在那里保留了很长时间。

sentences.en: But that's also something that's deeply ingrained in their sense of being of English liberties.
sentences.zh: 但这同样是他们对英国式自由感中根深蒂固的一部分。

sentences.en: That isn't they wouldn't have regarded that as something that's entirely new.
sentences.zh: 他们不会认为这是什么全新的东西。

sentences.en: They would have said, well, we've always had religious liberty or we thought we had.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，好吧，我们一直拥有宗教自由，或者我们以为我们有。

sentences.en: And the American Revolution has given it an impetus.
sentences.zh: 而美国革命给了它一种推动力。

sentences.en: And it's focused, you know, the Church of England and the church establishment was clearly associated in a place like Virginia,
sentences.zh: 而且它很集中，你知道，英国国教和教会体制在弗吉尼亚这样的地方显然是联系在一起的，

sentences.en: which had an established Anglican church associated with Tories and support for the king.
sentences.zh: 那里有既定的圣公会，与托利党和对国王的支持联系在一起。

sentences.en: And so they were delegitimized.
sentences.zh: 所以他们失去了合法性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's that great thing from Jefferson.
sentences.zh: 所以杰斐逊有那句名言。

sentences.en: It does mean no injury for my neighbor to say there are 20 gods or no god.
sentences.zh: “说有二十个神或没有神，对我邻居造成的伤害微乎其微。”

sentences.en: It neither picks my pocket nor breaks my leg.
sentences.zh: “它既不会掏走我的钱包，也不会打断我的腿。”

sentences.en: And I guess only someone who's been through a very violent war could maybe have made that made that case.
sentences.zh: 我想只有经历过一场非常残酷战争的人，才可能提出这样的论点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Thomas Jefferson himself had not actually been through a violent war in France.
sentences.zh: 所以托马斯·杰斐逊本人实际上并没有在法国经历过残酷的战争。

sentences.en: But yes, no, but I take your point.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，不，我明白你的意思。

sentences.en: But Jefferson's sort of performative secularism was not typical.
sentences.zh: 但杰斐逊那种表演性的世俗主义并不典型。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, most of the rest, I mean, Jefferson did say he was a deiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，其余大多数人，我是说，杰斐逊确实说过他是自然神论者。

sentences.en: And Tom Paine, of course, was certainly performatively non-religious.
sentences.zh: 当然，汤姆·潘恩肯定是以表演性的方式表现出非宗教倾向。

sentences.en: But not the rest of them.
sentences.zh: 但其他人并非如此。

sentences.en: The rest of them were all very pious church attending Presbyterians or Congregationalists.
sentences.zh: 其余的人都是非常虔诚的、去教堂做礼拜的长老会教徒或公理会教徒。

sentences.en: But Jefferson is a kind of sign of how far that can be pushed and that kind of brief window where it's possible to establish a new country on broadly Enlightenment principles.
sentences.zh: 但杰斐逊是一个标志，表明这种思想可以被推到多远，以及那个短暂的窗口期，即有可能在广泛的启蒙原则基础上建立一个新国家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Tom, you love Jefferson, but I can tell from the way that Adam uses the word performatively.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你很喜欢杰斐逊，但我能从亚当使用“表演性”这个词的方式中听出来。

sentences.en: I mean, he's the rankest of hypocrites.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他是个彻头彻尾的伪君子。

sentences.en: Oh, he is.
sentences.zh: 哦，他确实是。

sentences.en: He's a terrible man.
sentences.zh: 他是个可怕的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He ranks Tom with Bosie Douglas, John Lennon and Virginia Woolf as absolute enemies, sworn foes of the rest of history and some of the worst people who've ever lived.
sentences.zh: 他把汤姆与博西·道格拉斯、约翰·列侬和弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫并列，称他们为绝对的敌人，是历史剩余部分的死敌，也是有史以来最糟糕的人。

sentences.en: Now, I don't include John Lennon in that.
sentences.zh: 现在，我可没把约翰·列侬包括在内。

sentences.en: Before we move on to the to the future for the United States, there is, of course, one other country in North America that was created by these years.
sentences.zh: 在我们继续讨论美国的未来之前，当然，在北美还有另一个国家是在这些年里创建的。

sentences.en: And that is Canada.
sentences.zh: 那就是加拿大。

sentences.en: Is that too strong to say that this is the foundational moment of Canada?
sentences.zh: 说这是加拿大的奠基时刻，是否太夸张了？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I mean, Canada as an entity doesn't exist quite at this point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，加拿大作为一个实体在此时还并不完全存在。

sentences.en: But by definition, it exists because it's British North America.
sentences.zh: 但从定义上讲，它存在，因为它是英属北美。

sentences.en: And that's what people begin to refer to.
sentences.zh: 而这正是人们开始称呼它的方式。

sentences.en: It's British North America.
sentences.zh: 它是英属北美。

sentences.en: And everything that happens in British North America is also happening in the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且英属北美发生的一切也正在美国发生。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: it's a place of relative religious freedom and relatively high levels of political participation and access to land and wars with indigenous people and stories of exploitation.
sentences.zh: 它是一个拥有相对宗教自由、相对高水平政治参与、获得土地的机会、与原住民的战争以及剥削故事的地方。

sentences.en: What it doesn't have is slavery and it doesn't have a Republican constitution, but it develops and flourishes and prospers.
sentences.zh: 它没有奴隶制，也没有共和宪法，但它在发展、繁荣和昌盛。

sentences.en: And Canadian history begins at this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以加拿大历史从这一刻开始。

sentences.en: So that's Canada, the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是加拿大，美国。

sentences.en: So suddenly the United States, 1783, its independence has been recognized by Britain, which must seem like an absolutely extraordinary moment.
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，1783年的美国，其独立得到了英国的承认，这一定是一个绝对非凡的时刻。

sentences.en: Of course, they've thought of themselves as independent since the mid-1770s, but now they have it de jure as well as de facto.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们从18世纪70年代中期起就认为自己是独立的，但现在他们不仅在事实上，而且在法律上拥有了独立。

sentences.en: But is the United States a nation at that point?
sentences.zh: 但美国在那个时候是一个国家吗？

sentences.en: Surely it's just 13 different colonies in an uneasy confederation.
sentences.zh: 肯定只是一个不安定的邦联中的13个不同的殖民地。

sentences.en: In an uneasy confederation, in a dangerous world, with no template that they can follow.
sentences.zh: 在一个不安定的邦联中，在一个危险的世界里，没有他们可以遵循的模板。

sentences.en: Well, ancient Rome, perhaps?
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许是古罗马？

sentences.en: Well, they're looking to ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们正在向古罗马寻求借鉴。

sentences.en: Some of them are even looking at Swiss republics, the Dutch republic.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人甚至在研究瑞士共和国、荷兰共和国。

sentences.en: And there are historical precedents that the ancient ones are the most relevant.
sentences.zh: 而且有历史先例，古老的先例是最相关的。

sentences.en: Because the assumption is, at this point in European society, that republics basically implode.
sentences.zh: 因为在欧洲社会的这一点上，人们的假设是共和国基本上会内爆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the assumption, that they're inherently unstable.
sentences.zh: 这就是假设，它们本质上是不稳定的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, I mean, they are unstable at first, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，它们起初是不稳定的，不是吗？

sentences.en: They've got Shays' Rebellion.
sentences.zh: 他们有谢司起义。

sentences.en: They've got lots of local issues unresolved.
sentences.zh: 他们有很多未解决的地方性问题。

sentences.en: They've got the issue of the Native Americans on the frontier.
sentences.zh: 他们有边境上的美洲原住民问题。

sentences.en: Who knows that the French might not come back?
sentences.zh: 谁知道法国人会不会回来？

sentences.en: The British might come back.
sentences.zh: 英国人可能会回来。

sentences.en: And they have no leadership, no capital, no government, really, do they, at this point?
sentences.zh: 而且在这一点上，他们真的没有领导层、没有首都、没有政府，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, effectively, the Articles of Confederation are really more like a kind of peace treaty among these 13 newly independent states with no proper executive.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，《邦联条例》更像是这13个新独立国家之间的一种和平条约，没有真正的行政部门。

sentences.en: They theoretically have treaty-making power, but they've got no tax-raising ability.
sentences.zh: 他们理论上有缔约权，但没有征税能力。

sentences.en: So it's a very shaky beginning for the newly United States.
sentences.zh: 所以对于新生的美国来说，这是一个非常不稳定的开端。

sentences.en: And then what, I mean, anybody who's seen the musical Hamilton will know that Alexander Hamilton, who we've not mentioned at all, and James Madison,
sentences.zh: 那么，我是说，任何看过音乐剧《汉密尔顿》的人都会知道，亚历山大·汉密尔顿——我们根本没提过他——还有詹姆斯·麦迪逊，

sentences.en: who I think we mentioned in passing, that they are two of the key figures in creating a kind of national government and moving towards a constitution and a much stronger executive.
sentences.zh: 我想我们顺便提过他，他们是创建某种国家政府并迈向宪法和更强有力的行政部门的两个关键人物。

sentences.en: A monarch, effectively, an elected monarch.
sentences.zh: 一个君主，实际上，一个民选君主。

sentences.en: Like, what is it that provokes them to do that?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么促使他们这样做呢？

sentences.en: And why does everybody else, having been anti-government and anti-British power and all that stuff for so long, why do they suddenly say, OK, well, now we need to – is it fear?
sentences.zh: 为什么其他人，在长期反政府、反英国势力之后，突然说，好吧，现在我们需要——是恐惧吗？

sentences.en: Is it – what is it?
sentences.zh: 是——那是什么？

sentences.en: Fundamentally, it is fear.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，是恐惧。

sentences.en: But there is, effectively, a revolution in favour of government, to use a phrase that other historians have used.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，用其他历史学家使用过的一个短语来说，确实发生了一场支持政府的革命。

sentences.en: Well, it's their government, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是他们自己的政府，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the key difference.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是关键的区别。

sentences.en: It's not government that's being practised on the other side of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 这不是在海洋彼岸实施的政府。

sentences.en: It's their government, and they can choose it.
sentences.zh: 这是他们自己的政府，他们可以选择它。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And, you know, John Adams said around about the time of the Declaration of Independence that there's something odious in a government a thousand leagues away.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，约翰·亚当斯在《独立宣言》发表前后曾说，在千里之外的政府中，有些东西是令人厌恶的。

sentences.en: And this whole movement is about, yes, taking back control and creating a government of our own.
sentences.zh: 而整个运动就是关于，是的，夺回控制权并建立我们自己的政府。

sentences.en: Well, they have representation, and so now they can have taxation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们有了代表权，所以现在他们可以纳税了。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: But there's a continuing of needs about it.
sentences.zh: 但关于它还有一种持续的需求。

sentences.en: I mean, without getting into the whole – all the sort of – the dotting the last I's and crossing the T's of the constitution-making, there's a tension between federalists,
sentences.zh: 我是说，在不深入探讨所有那些——宪法制定过程中所有那些细节的情况下，联邦主义者之间存在一种紧张关系，

sentences.en: which is Hamilton, Madison, and co.
sentences.zh: 也就是汉密尔顿、麦迪逊等人。

sentences.en: So, anti-federalists, which is Jefferson, about whether or not there should be a powerful state, whether there should be a central government,
sentences.zh: 所以，反联邦主义者，也就是杰斐逊，关于是否应该有一个强大的国家，是否应该有一个中央政府，

sentences.en: whether you should just let the states get on with it.
sentences.zh: 是否应该让各州自行其是。

sentences.en: And would it be too strong to say that that runs all that argument,
sentences.zh: 说那贯穿了所有争论是否太夸张了，

sentences.en: which is happening in the aftermath of the Treaty of Paris and then the adoption of the constitution in Philadelphia in 1787?
sentences.zh: 那场争论发生在《巴黎条约》之后，以及1787年在费城通过宪法之后？

sentences.en: That runs all the way through American history, or is that – am I just being too simplistic and back-projecting current American political debates to the 18th century?
sentences.zh: 那贯穿了整个美国历史，还是说——我只是太简单化了，把当前的美国政治辩论投射回了18世纪？

sentences.en: The nature of the debate changes, obviously, over the generations, but that fundamental tension is there right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 辩论的性质显然在几代人中发生了变化，但那种根本的紧张关系从一开始就存在。

sentences.en: And there's huge unease and opposition to the project of creating a stronger central government.
sentences.zh: 而且对于建立一个更强大的中央政府的计划，存在巨大的不安和反对。

sentences.en: There's this huge discomfort with the presidency in particular as a strong executive with prerogative powers that far exceed what George III had.
sentences.zh: 特别是对总统职位作为一种强大的行政部门感到极度不适，其特权远远超过了乔治三世所拥有的权力。

sentences.en: A kind of model of executive, a single executive based on a kind of Stuart conception of kingship,
sentences.zh: 一种行政模式，一种基于某种斯图亚特王朝君主制概念的单一行政长官，

sentences.en: admittedly with the pretty massive caveat that the person is elected rather than has any notion of being divinely appointed and being hereditary.
sentences.zh: 当然，有一个非常巨大的警告，即此人是选举产生的，而不是有任何神授或世袭的概念。

sentences.en: But nevertheless,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，

sentences.en: a model of the constitution that is like a kind of pre-glorious revolution English version of the English constitution with a strong executive and a separately elected,
sentences.zh: 一种宪法模式，就像某种光荣革命前的英国版英国宪法，拥有强大的行政部门和单独选举产生的、

sentences.en: separately selected legislature.
sentences.zh: 单独选出的立法机构。

sentences.en: But again, there is a slight hint of the Roman about it because you have the figure of Washington, this great general who has led his people, his fellow citizens,
sentences.zh: 但同样，它有一点罗马式的意味，因为你有华盛顿这个人物，这位伟大的将军，他领导了他的同胞，他的公民同僚，

sentences.en: and then he returns to his plough.
sentences.zh: 然后他回到了他的犁旁。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the image of it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是它的形象。

sentences.en: George III himself had said, if Washington does that, then he is the greatest man in history, or words to that effect.
sentences.zh: 乔治三世本人曾说，如果华盛顿这样做，那么他就是历史上最伟大的人，或者类似的话。

sentences.en: And he does.
sentences.zh: 而他确实这样做了。

sentences.en: He goes back to Mount Vernon and farms, or at least he gets his enslaved people to farm for him.
sentences.zh: 他回到弗农山庄务农，或者至少他让他的奴隶为他务农。

sentences.en: So in a sense, when the Americans are thinking, you know, we want this kind of monarchical president,
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，当美国人思考时，你知道，我们想要这种君主制的总统，

sentences.en: they can do that with a degree of confidence that they have the ideal candidate to hand, a figure of antique Roman virtue.
sentences.zh: 他们可以带着一定程度的信心这样做，因为他们手头有理想的候选人，一个具有古代罗马美德的人物。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think we probably haven't emphasized Washington enough, actually.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们可能实际上还没有足够强调华盛顿。

sentences.en: The figure that Washington became through the war.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿在战争中成为的人物。

sentences.en: I mean, Dominic, you said, is this a nation?
sentences.zh: 我是说，多米尼克，你说，这是一个国家吗？

sentences.en: I mean, who knows whether it's, I mean, you can argue about what makes a nation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，谁知道它是否是，我是说，你可以争论是什么造就了一个国家。

sentences.en: Of course, historians spend a lot of time doing so.
sentences.zh: 当然，历史学家花了很多时间这样做。

sentences.en: But if anything has made a nation, it's the experience of war.
sentences.zh: 但如果有什么造就了一个国家，那就是战争的经历。

sentences.en: And it's the figure of George Washington as the embodiment of the American cause with his honor and his integrity and his apparent inability to ever tell a lie.
sentences.zh: 而且是乔治·华盛顿这个人物，作为美国事业的化身，带着他的荣誉、他的正直以及他似乎永远无法撒谎的特质。

sentences.en: So that's a fascinating question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个引人入胜的问题。

sentences.en: So that raises an interesting question about Washington.
sentences.zh: 所以这提出了一个关于华盛顿的有趣问题。

sentences.en: Are the Americans fortunate to have somebody like Washington, who gives them a focal point, a hero, a figure around which the nation can coalesce?
sentences.zh: 美国人是否很幸运拥有像华盛顿这样的人，他给了他们一个焦点、一个英雄、一个国家可以围绕其凝聚的人物？

sentences.en: Or were they always going to produce somebody like that onto whom they could project those qualities?
sentences.zh: 还是说他们注定会塑造出那样一个人，好将那些品质投射到他身上？

sentences.en: Do you think, Adam?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，亚当？

sentences.en: I mean, should we, in other words, is Washington a creation of the kind of national imagination?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，换句话说，华盛顿是否是某种民族想象的产物？

sentences.en: Well, there's certainly something in that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: There was evidently a yearning for some kind of replacement father figure.
sentences.zh: 当时显然渴望出现某种替代性的父亲形象。

sentences.en: They got rid of one George, but fortunately they had another George ready to, in some respects, step into the shoes of the deposed king.
sentences.zh: 他们摆脱了一个乔治，但幸运的是，他们还有另一个乔治准备好，在某些方面接替那位被废黜国王的位置。

sentences.en: They were fortunate that Washington was such a good figure on which to project their desires and hopes.
sentences.zh: 他们很幸运，华盛顿是一个非常好的投射对象，可以承载他们的渴望与希望。

sentences.en: But I think, I mean, I think that question massively underplays the moral stature of Washington as a political leader.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我是说，我认为这个问题大大低估了华盛顿作为政治领袖的道德高度。

sentences.en: Because if you think of the English Revolution, the American Revolution, the French Revolution, the English Revolution throws up Cromwell.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你看看英国革命、美国革命、法国革命，英国革命涌现出了克伦威尔。

sentences.en: The French Revolution throws up Napoleon, both of whom essentially become dictatorial figures.
sentences.zh: 法国革命涌现出了拿破仑，两人本质上都成了独裁者。

sentences.en: Washington doesn't.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿则不然。

sentences.en: And that then establishes the whole kind of tenor of the American presidency.
sentences.zh: 这确立了美国总统制的整体基调。

sentences.en: And therefore, the character of the United States, not just as a republic, but in the very long run, a democracy as well.
sentences.zh: 也因此确立了美国的性格，不仅作为一个共和国，从长远来看，也作为一个民主国家。

sentences.en: Strongly agree with that, Tom.
sentences.zh: 非常同意这一点，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think Washington was a great man.
sentences.zh: 我认为华盛顿是一位伟人。

sentences.en: And I think he probably is a figure that we need to recognise more for his role in all of these events and in the creation of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他可能是一个我们需要更多地认可他在所有这些事件以及美国创建过程中所扮演角色的历史人物。

sentences.en: Yes, I don't know who we is in that sentence either.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也不知道那句话里的“我们”指的是谁。

sentences.en: Well, I guess, Adam, that you might be talking about your academic peers, the scholars who study the American Revolution and the origins of American history.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我猜，亚当，你可能是在说你的学术同行，那些研究美国革命和美国历史起源的学者们。

sentences.en: Because, of course, this is now, you know, it's not just a matter for scholars, is it?
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，这现在，你知道，不仅仅是学者们的事了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's highly contested political territory.
sentences.zh: 这是一个高度争议的政治领域。

sentences.en: And the idea that Washington might be criticised more for owning slaves, say, than for defeating the British,
sentences.zh: 而且，华盛顿可能更多地因为拥有奴隶而不是因为击败英国人而受到批评，这种观点，

sentences.en: which would have been kind of unheard of idea, maybe even 20 years ago, 30 years ago, is now quite current in America.
sentences.zh: 在20年前、30年前可能还是闻所未闻的，现在在美国却相当普遍。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, at every stage in this story and in all the stories that you two tell on your podcast, there is huge contingency.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个故事的每个阶段，以及你们俩在播客中讲述的所有故事中，都存在巨大的偶然性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's what you two do so well is to tell a story always with a kind of sense of alternative possibilities.
sentences.zh: 而你们俩做得最好的地方，就是总是带着一种对替代可能性的感知来讲述故事。

sentences.en: And that's what history is.
sentences.zh: 这就是历史的本质。

sentences.en: And by contingency, of course, we don't mean just sheer luck.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所说的偶然性，指的不仅仅是纯粹的运气。

sentences.en: We mean the kind of awareness of other options at every moment.
sentences.zh: 我们指的是在每一刻对其他选择的某种觉知。

sentences.en: And George Washington's personality shaped the key moments, shaped that contingency in ways that benefited the future stability and, in some respects,
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿的个性塑造了关键时刻，以某种方式塑造了那种偶然性，从而造福了新生的美国未来的稳定，并在某些方面，

sentences.en: the openness and liberal freedom of the newly created United States.
sentences.zh: 造福了新生的美国所拥有的开放与自由。

sentences.en: But can I ask then, the corollary of that is that if the stature of Washington is kind of like the foundation stone of the myth of America's beginnings,
sentences.zh: 但我能问一下吗，随之而来的推论是，如果华盛顿的地位就像美国起源神话的基石，

sentences.en: and I don't use myth in a pejorative sense.
sentences.zh: 我并不是贬义地使用“神话”这个词。

sentences.en: I mean, a myth is something that is powerful and can be ennobling and inspiring.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，神话是一种强大的东西，可以起到提升和激励的作用。

sentences.en: But if that foundation stone starts to kind of be, you know, you start to shift it, you tug at it, you kind of question it,
sentences.zh: 但如果那块基石开始，你知道，你开始动摇它，拉扯它，质疑它，

sentences.en: is that improving Americans' understandings of their past and therefore opening up new opportunities for kind of making a better state?
sentences.zh: 这是否在改善美国人对他们过去的理解，从而为建设一个更好的国家开辟了新的机会？

sentences.en: Or is it by damaging the kind of the origin myth, are you damaging the coherence and the fabric of the American Republic as it exists now?
sentences.zh: 还是说，通过破坏那种起源神话，你也在破坏现存美国共和国的连贯性和结构？

sentences.en: I mean, that's a massive question, but it is one that seems to shadow a lot of the debate in contemporary America about the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个宏大的问题，但它似乎笼罩着当代美国关于美国革命的许多辩论。

sentences.en: There's a lot of deep discomfort in the contemporary United States with a story of the national origins, which is built around great men and great white men and great white men,
sentences.zh: 在当代美国，人们对国家起源的故事感到深深的不安，这个故事是围绕着伟人，伟大的白人，伟大的白人建立起来的，

sentences.en: many of whom were the owners of, claimed to be the owners of other human beings.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人是奴隶主，或者声称自己是其他人类的主人。

sentences.en: Among whom was Washington himself and Jefferson, who wrote the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 其中包括华盛顿本人和撰写《独立宣言》的杰斐逊。

sentences.en: And James Madison, who was the principal author of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 还有宪法的主要起草者詹姆斯·麦迪逊。

sentences.en: And Patrick Henry, who said, give me liberty or give me death.
sentences.zh: 以及说过“不自由，毋宁死”的帕特里克·亨利。

sentences.en: There's deep discomfort about that.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到深深的不安。

sentences.en: And you can understand why.
sentences.zh: 你可以理解为什么。

sentences.en: I mean, you can understand why, can't you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以理解为什么，不是吗？

sentences.en: And in a way, the remarkable thing is that it's taken until this point in the 21st century for that kind of critique to have the popular purchase that it has now.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，令人瞩目的是，直到21世纪的今天，这种批判才获得了现在这样广泛的认可。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, you mentioned in a previous episode, the New York Times 1619 project.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，你在之前的一集里提到了《纽约时报》的“1619项目”。

sentences.en: And the fundamental value of the 1619 project is to challenge that old framing in a very direct way.
sentences.zh: 而“1619项目”的基本价值在于以一种非常直接的方式挑战那种旧的框架。

sentences.en: And so it's directly and deliberately replacing 1776 with 1619, the date at which unfree black people were landed in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 所以它直接且刻意地用1619年——即失去自由的黑人被运抵弗吉尼亚的日期——取代了1776年。

sentences.en: And saying that that is the real origin moment of the United States rather than 1776.
sentences.zh: 并声称那才是美国真正的起源时刻，而不是1776年。

sentences.en: Of course, they're both still operating within the same frame, which is that there has to be a moment of origin.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们都在同一个框架内运作，即必须有一个起源时刻。

sentences.en: And in both cases, that 1776 or 1619 were in some teleological sense leading towards the creation of something called the United States.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，无论是1776年还是1619年，在某种目的论意义上，都指向了所谓美国的创建。

sentences.en: So last question, Adam, for you, because you have been, I should say, for those listeners who have listened to this over two weeks, you've been listening to this over two weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以最后一个问题，亚当，问你，因为你一直，我应该说，对于那些在过去两周里听这个节目的听众来说，你们已经听了两周了。

sentences.en: But Adam has been doing this over basically the course of four hours in one go.
sentences.zh: 但亚当基本上是在四个小时内一口气完成的。

sentences.en: Well, so have you two.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你们俩也是。

sentences.en: In fact, I haven't been dubbed in.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我没有被后期配音。

sentences.en: We've just been following up the questions, do you?
sentences.zh: 我们只是在跟进问题，是吗？

sentences.en: It's not like Megan and Harris podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这不像梅根和哈里的播客。

sentences.en: We're there with you.
sentences.zh: 我们和你在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah, we don't do the questions separately.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们不会分开提问。

sentences.en: So, Adam, where does the story of the American Revolution go from here?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，美国革命的故事从这里走向何方？

sentences.en: Because, of course, it's so contested at the moment.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，它目前争议很大。

sentences.en: People argue about precisely these things that you've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 人们争论的正是你一直在谈论的这些事情。

sentences.en: But as you look forward, how do you think people will – I mean, do you think the patriotic narrative that we see now when we go to Boston, we do the Freedom Trail,
sentences.zh: 但当你展望未来时，你认为人们会——我的意思是，你认为我们现在去波士顿，走“自由之路”时所看到的爱国叙事，

sentences.en: or you go to Mount Vernon, or you walk around Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 或者你去弗农山庄，或者你在华盛顿特区漫步，

sentences.en: and you see all the sites, do you think that will effectively survive?
sentences.zh: 看到所有的遗迹，你认为这会有效地存续下去吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's challenged in The New York Times and in the Academy, but effectively it's too rooted now in the American imagination.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在《纽约时报》和学术界受到挑战，但实际上它现在已经深深扎根于美国的想象之中了。

sentences.en: Or do you think there will be more changes to come in the 21st century?
sentences.zh: 还是你认为在21世纪还会有更多的变化？

sentences.en: I don't know, but I think that if the American Republic is going to survive in something like its present form, and of course it is the oldest continuous,
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但我认为如果美国共和国要以某种类似于目前的形式存续下去，当然它是最古老的连续体，

sentences.en: and it's an incredibly old country, the United States, with the world's oldest codified constitution.
sentences.zh: 而且美国是一个极其古老的国家，拥有世界上最古老的成文宪法。

sentences.en: If it's going to continue, then it needs its origin myth.
sentences.zh: 如果它要继续存在，那么它就需要它的起源神话。

sentences.en: And the origin myth has always evolved.
sentences.zh: 而起源神话一直在演变。

sentences.en: It's never a static thing.
sentences.zh: 它从来不是静止的东西。

sentences.en: And there should be a way, and there is a way,
sentences.zh: 应该有一种方式，而且确实有一种方式，

sentences.en: of telling the story of the American Revolution and the founding of the republic and those ringing principles of the Declaration of Independence and the value of republicanism and the commitment to popular participation in politics and openness and the commitment to being an asylum for mankind and all of these things.
sentences.zh: 来讲述美国革命和共和国建立的故事，讲述《独立宣言》中那些响亮的原则，讲述共和主义的价值，讲述对大众参与政治的承诺，讲述开放性，以及致力于成为人类避难所的承诺，所有这些事情。

sentences.en: There should be a way of telling that story in a way that is more inclusive than has been the case over most of the last two centuries.
sentences.zh: 应该有一种方式来讲述那个故事，使其比过去两个世纪的大部分时间里更具包容性。

sentences.en: And the reason why I think the 1619 project has been so challenging to some of my academic colleagues of an older generation is because of their fear that by changing the frame so dramatically to focus on the question of race and slavery,
sentences.zh: 我认为“1619项目”之所以让一些老一辈的学术同行感到如此具有挑战性，是因为他们担心通过如此剧烈地改变框架来聚焦于种族和奴隶制问题，

sentences.en: then everything else will go.
sentences.zh: 那么其他一切都会随之而去。

sentences.en: And there are certainly academic colleagues of mine in the United States on the left and generally of a younger generation who want to do that,
sentences.zh: 在美国，确实有我的学术同行，左翼的，通常是年轻一代的，他们想要这样做，

sentences.en: who want to throw out the whole concept of the nation state and who see the United States as fundamentally corrupted and can't imagine any true emancipation within the context of the policy that was created in 1776 or 1787.
sentences.zh: 他们想要抛弃整个民族国家的概念，他们认为美国从根本上是腐败的，无法想象在1776年或1787年创建的政体背景下实现任何真正的解放。

sentences.en: There are those people.
sentences.zh: 确实有这样的人。

sentences.en: Well, and from the point of view of us in Britain,
sentences.zh: 嗯，从我们英国人的角度来看，

sentences.en: one of the weird corollaries of this narrative that basically the American colonists in the War of Independence were fighting to keep slavery is to cast the British Empire rather implausibly as an agent of abolitionism,
sentences.zh: 这种叙事的一个奇怪推论是，基本上美国殖民者在独立战争中是为了维持奴隶制而战，这不可思议地将大英帝国塑造成了废奴主义的代理人，

sentences.en: which in due course, of course, it does become, but not at this point, right?
sentences.zh: 虽然大英帝国最终确实成为了废奴主义者，但不是在那个时候，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't get British imperialism off the hook to say that actually they were the goodies in this, because that's clearly not true.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，说他们实际上是其中的好人并不能让英国帝国主义摆脱干系，因为这显然不是事实。

sentences.en: There are lots of ways in which the 1619 project can be and has been critiqued.
sentences.zh: “1619项目”有很多可以被批评的地方，也确实受到了批评。

sentences.en: And insofar as the original 1619 articles suggested that defense of slavery was a principal reason for the American Revolution and that there was a deep anxiety on the part of American slaveholders that the British Empire was turning to anti-slavery,
sentences.zh: 就最初的1619年文章暗示捍卫奴隶制是美国革命的主要原因，以及美国奴隶主对大英帝国转向反奴隶制感到深深焦虑而言，

sentences.en: that is a great exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 那是非常夸大的。

sentences.en: I mean, as we discussed,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我们讨论过的，

sentences.en: it was certainly true in the Caroliners and Virginia that plenty of slaveholders were terrified at the prospect of the British using enslaved people against them.
sentences.zh: 在卡罗来纳和弗吉尼亚，确实有很多奴隶主对英国人利用被奴役者来对付他们感到恐惧。

sentences.en: It is not true, generally speaking, to say the American Revolution was fought in defense of slavery.
sentences.zh: 但笼统地说美国革命是为了捍卫奴隶制而战，是不真实的。

sentences.en: There are people who directly make the connection between the secession of the 13 American colonies in the 1770s and the secession of the southern states in 1861.
sentences.zh: 有些人直接将1770年代13个美国殖民地的分裂与1861年南方各州的分裂联系起来。

sentences.en: That is hugely overdrawn, in my opinion,
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这被大大夸大了，

sentences.en: not least because while in the 1860s there was a big anti-slavery movement in the northern states and there were genuine reasons for southern slaveholders to think that their security,
sentences.zh: 不仅因为虽然在1860年代北方各州有强大的反奴隶制运动，而且南方奴隶主有真正的理由认为他们的安全，

sentences.en: their slave property would be undermined within the Union, that just wasn't true to anything like the same degree in the 1770s.
sentences.zh: 他们的奴隶财产会在联邦内受到损害，但在1770年代，情况根本不是这样。

sentences.en: There was an anti-slavery movement in Britain, there was an anti-slavery movement in Philadelphia and in New England.
sentences.zh: 当时英国有反奴隶制运动，费城和新英格兰也有反奴隶制运动。

sentences.en: It was not one that was going to overwhelm the slaveholders' security had they remained within the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 如果他们留在英帝国之内，那股力量并不会压倒奴隶主的安全。

sentences.en: What threatened their slave property was participating in rebellion.
sentences.zh: 真正威胁到他们奴隶财产的是参与叛乱。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。
